ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.proof_nl:
Assume the standing definitions are
F_n(x) = floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
and
H_n = sum_{k=1}^n 1/k.
Let x satisfy (n-1)/n <= x < 1.

For each k with 1 <= k < n, we have
k(n-1)/n <= kx < k,
so in fact k-1 < kx < k. Hence floor(kx) = k-1.
For k = n, we have
n-1 <= nx < n,
so floor(nx) = n-1.

Therefore
F_n(x) = (n-1) - sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (k-1)/k - (n-1)/n.
Now
sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (k-1)/k = sum_{k=1}^{n-1} (1 - 1/k) = (n-1) - sum_{k=1}^{n-1} 1/k,
so
F_n(x) = (n-1) - [(n-1) - sum_{k=1}^{n-1} 1/k] - (n-1)/n
= sum_{k=1}^{n-1} 1/k - (n-1)/n
= H_{n-1} - (n-1)/n.
Using H_n = H_{n-1} + 1/n, we get
H_{n-1} - (n-1)/n = H_n - 1.
Thus F_n(x) = H_n - 1 for every x in [(n-1)/n, 1).
payload.role_in_assembly: Shows that the candidate maximizing interval actually attains the global upper bound.
